conviction_note: I recovered an actual option-implied move from the capture - 11.55% for the weekly expiring 2026-09-04, captured at 15:16Z on the event date and therefore pre-print - which almost exactly matches the 11.08% historical median, so there is no magnitude dislocation; I take a positive point estimate inside that band because two independent, low-circulation inputs (LinkedIn headcount accelerating 4.0% over three months with 262 open roles, and RBC calling the FY27 guide conservative) point the same way while the five-session run-in of -7.45% is a sector de-rating rather than anything company-specific.

findings.finding: Alternative data shows Samsara accelerating hiring into the print: LinkedIn headcount up 4.0% over three months to 5,745 (against 2,895 in the most recent official filings) with 262 active job postings - and AltIndex's own framing is that headcount leads revenue, companies hiring before acceleration and cutting before disappointment.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/71fcfd6ecce3406e232cc422335b088aa655d78c.txt (snapshots/20260903T151623Z.json item 13, captured 15:16Z on the event date, pre-print for an after-the-close release)
findings.why_not_priced: Headcount and job-posting series are alt-data behind a screening product, never carried by a wire and absent from all six preview items in the same sweep (StockStory, Yahoo, tikr, stocktitan, simplywall.st, saastr) - every one of those frames the print as consensus revenue and ARR. A company adding 4% to its workforce in the quarter it is about to report is not preparing to guide down. If it were priced, the stock would not have fallen 7.5% in the five sessions into the event.
findings.independence: A separate item in the same sweep, from marketscreener, records RBC characterising Samsara's raised fiscal-2027 guidance as 'somewhat conservative' - a different source pointing at the same beatable-guide conclusion: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/samsara-s-higher-fiscal-2027-guidance-somewhat-conservative-rbc-says-ce7f5dddd08bf424

findings.finding: Samsara Beyond 2026, the company's customer conference, ran on 24-25 June 2026 with a broad wave of AI-for-physical-operations product announcements - i.e. squarely inside the fiscal second quarter now being reported, so the bookings and pipeline effect of that launch cycle lands in this print and in the guide that follows it.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/b0905a53065825f9d085b78d52ee2f2e472e46b3.txt (snapshots/20260903T151623Z.json item 14), datePublished 2026-06-24/25; company source at snapshots item 15
findings.why_not_priced: The launches themselves were covered in June and are priced as news. What is not priced is the timing relative to the reporting period - none of the six previews in this capture mentions Beyond at all, and a mid-quarter product wave in a land-and-expand telematics model shows up as net-new ARR and as a guidance input, not as a June headline. The tape between the conference and the print is +1.4% over twenty sessions, i.e. nothing was paid for it.
findings.independence: The company's own announcement blog is captured separately in the same sweep - https://www.samsara.com/blog/announcing-new-innovations-to-reduce-risk-increase-efficiency-and-digitally-transform-operations

findings.finding: The five-session -7.45% fall into the print is sector, not company: the same sweep captures a piece arguing 'The SaaS Rout of 2026 Is Even Worse Than You Think - for the first time ever software now trades at a discount to the S&P 500', and the last Samsara print (2026-06-04) fell 1.16% despite 31% revenue growth, a raised FY27 guide to $2.013bn and a third consecutive GAAP profit.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the weakest of the three because it is a framing argument rather than a datapoint, and it cuts both ways - a de-rating sector can keep de-rating. Its value is that it identifies the -7.45% run-in as multiple compression on a name whose three prints before the last one produced +17.4%, +11.1% and +19.5%, which is why I do not read the run-in as informed selling.
findings.independence: A JPMorgan Q3-2026 software sector report is captured in the same sweep and would corroborate or refute the de-rating claim, but I did not extract a figure from it - https://www.jpmorgan.com/content/dam/jpmorgan/documents/cb/insights/outlook/jpm-q3-2026-software-market-trends-report.pdf

baseline_tension: It cuts against the five-session run-in (-7.45%) and agrees with the twenty-session run-in (+1.4%) and with the three-out-of-four positive reactions before the last one; on magnitude it agrees with the baseline exactly, because the recovered 11.55% implied move matches the 11.08% median.
corpus_limits: The baseline states no implied move is recoverable; in this one case the capture happens to contain a marketchameleon/optionslam page stored at 15:16Z on the event date giving an 11.55% weekly and 14.54% monthly implied move, which I used for sizing only and which is pre-print for an after-the-close release. Four of the sweep's URLs failed to fetch, including both insider-selling items and the RBC guidance note, so three of my supporting points are headline-and-slug only. This is an amc print, so the 2026-09-03 sweeps and price bar are pre-event and admissible; no item in this capture carried a non-empty tripwire_tells.
